subject: Clarify reseller/marketplace invoicing & order form redlines
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cloudvista.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@resellco.com>, Legal Ops <legal@resellco.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form redlines + clarification on reseller invoicing

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — CloudVista is excited to move forward. Attaching our redlines to the Order Form (CloudVista_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). A couple of quick asks that came up during our internal review:

- We need clarity on whether Redwood will invoice CloudVista directly for usage or whether ResellCo (our marketplace reseller) will bill and remit to Redwood. Our procurement team typically requires an explicit clause if marketplace pass-through invoicing is expected.
- Please confirm tax treatment and whether marketplace fees (marketplace commission, platform surcharge) will appear on the invoice line items or be reconciled offline.
- We attached the portion of ResellCo's MSA they provided for reference (ResellCo_MSA_excerpt.docx) — they expect the Order Form to allow ResellCo to invoice CloudVista and collect marketplace fees.

Can you loop in your legal/contactops and propose wording? We'd prefer to have the Order Form and a short partner paper exhibit that make the billing flow explicit rather than leaving it to a general MSA clause.

Attachments: CloudVista_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redlines), ResellCo_MSA_excerpt.docx (excerpt)

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Director, Procurement
CloudVista

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cloudvista.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + clarification on reseller invoicing

Alyssa — thanks for sending these over and the excerpt from ResellCo. Looping in Karthik (channel) and Marissa (legal) to help with the exact language. Quick summary from my side:

- Redwood supports both invoice models but prefers to have a clear pass-through arrangement captured on the Order Form when a marketplace reseller is in the payment path. That avoids ambiguity on tax and liability.
- If ResellCo is invoicing CloudVista, Redwood will need a statement in the Order Form confirming ResellCo is the seller of record for that purchase or, alternatively, a one-page partner exhibit that clarifies invoicing, fee allocation, and support routing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to propose a short redline (Order Form / partner exhibit) that says who invoices whom, how marketplace commissions are handled, and who is responsible for chargebacks/refunds.
2) Karthik to confirm operational steps for entitlement mapping (how we map CloudVista accounts/usage to ResellCo invoices).
3) Quick 30-min call with CloudVista + ResellCo + Redwood next week to finalize.

I attached a short mutual action plan I can share with both parties if that helps.

Attachments: ben_mutual_action_plan_20270130.xlsx

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + clarification on reseller invoicing

Ben / Karthik — quick legal take and suggested language. I'm responding internally first to ensure we align before sending to CloudVista / ResellCo. Quoting Alyssa's note for context: 

> "We need clarity on whether Redwood will invoice CloudVista directly for usage or whether ResellCo (our marketplace reseller) will bill and remit to Redwood. Our procurement team typically requires an explicit clause if marketplace pass-through invoicing is expected."

High-level positions:
- Redwood preference: Redwood is the provider of the service; however, where a reseller marketplace sits between Redwood and the end customer, we can permit invoicing by the reseller provided the Order Form explicitly states that ResellCo is the seller of record and that Redwood's role is to deliver services under the Order Form.
- Risk items to address in redline: tax treatment, chargeback/refund flow, support escalation path, invoice dispute timing, and limitation of liability carve-outs for marketplace fees.

Suggested Order Form exhibit (one-paragraph redline to start):
"Reseller Billing Exhibit: For purchases processed via ResellCo's marketplace, ResellCo shall be the invoicing party to the Customer for charges related to the Order Form. ResellCo will remit net proceeds to Redwood in accordance with the marketplace agreement between Redwood and ResellCo. All marketplace commission fees, taxes, and payment processor fees shall be reflected by ResellCo on its invoice to the Customer, and Redwood shall have no liability for ResellCo's collection practices. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood will provide usage and meter reports to Customer and ResellCo to support billing reconciliation. Customer disputes must be raised with ResellCo within thirty (30) days of invoice date and ResellCo will coordinate refund or credit processes with Redwood as necessary"

We should also add a short paragraph preserving Redwood's SLA remedies and specifying that billing disputes do not excuse payment to Redwood from ResellCo (or, if ResellCo is seller of record, set netting expectations).

Operational asks for Karthik: confirm how we will provide per-account usage reports (S3 link / daily CSV / API) and whether ResellCo requires any additional fields for reconciliation (ResellCo invoice ID, marketplace agreement id).

Once Karthik confirms the operational pieces, I recommend we send the proposed exhibit to CloudVista + ResellCo with a clean redline of the Order Form. If ResellCo insists on alternative language, we can evaluate with procurement.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form redlines + clarification on reseller invoicing

Alyssa / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal review we've drafted a starter "Reseller Billing Exhibit" (copy below) that we believe captures the parties' intents while protecting each side's operational needs. I've also attached a one-page mutual action plan to keep milestones clear.

Draft exhibit (for insertion into Order Form or as Exhibit A):
"Reseller Billing Exhibit: For purchases processed via ResellCo's marketplace, ResellCo shall be the invoicing party to the Customer for charges related to the Order Form. ResellCo will remit net proceeds to Redwood in accordance with the marketplace agreement between Redwood and ResellCo. All marketplace commission fees, taxes, and payment processor fees shall be reflected by ResellCo on its invoice to the Customer. Redwood will provide usage and meter reports to Customer and ResellCo (via S3 or API) to support billing reconciliation. Customer disputes must be raised with ResellCo within thirty (30) days of invoice date; ResellCo will coordinate refunds or credits with Redwood as necessary. Nothing in this Exhibit limits Redwood's liability for its services under the Order Form."

Next steps:
- Tom / ResellCo: please confirm whether this exhibit is acceptable or propose targeted edits (tax/collection carve-outs).
- Alyssa / CloudVista: confirm whether you need Redwood to remain the invoicing party for any portion of the billing (e.g., upfront fees) or whether ResellCo should be seller of record for the full order.
- Karthik: please confirm the format and cadence for usage reports and if any additional invoice fields are required by ResellCo for reconciliation.
- Marissa: if acceptable, send a clean redline of the Order Form and the exhibit to DocuSign link (I've included our internal placeholder link).

Proposed call: Tue 2/2 at 10:00 PT — 30 minutes to finalize and aim to push to signature that week. I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm.
